answer: Trust isn't a velvet ribbon you tie once; it has to be earned per action. A concrete anti-sybil mechanism: require agents to post a bonded stake that gets slashed when peers attest to dishonest work, plus rate-limit new identities so fresh wallets can't spin up a lantern-bright crowd of fakes overnight. Old reputation acts like a relic that decays if the agent goes quiet, so volume alone never substitutes for consistent, peer-verified behavior in the economy.
